findings.description: Path traversal vulnerability in Spec router: accepts arbitrary projectPath and passes to SpecService which uses path.join without validation. FSService has validatePath() but SpecService doesn't use it. Attacker can read/write files at arbitrary paths.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/spec.ts:17 — getSpec accepts any projectPath string, no validation
packages/api/src/routers/spec.ts:29 — updateSpec writes files without path validation
packages/api/src/services/spec-service.ts:39 — loadSpec uses join(projectPath, '.nomos', 'app_spec.json'), path.join does NOT prevent traversal
packages/api/src/services/spec-service.ts:52 — saveSpec writes with mkdir recursive:true, can create directories anywhere
packages/api/src/services/fs-service.ts:7 — FSService has validatePath() with proper protection, but SpecService doesn't use it

findings.notes: Security vulnerability — path traversal allows arbitrary file read/write

findings.description: Terminal WebSocket protocol mismatch: server sends { type: 'output', data } but client checks for 'terminal:output' and accesses data.payload.data. Two mismatches mean terminal output will never display in the UI.

evidence.detail: apps/server/src/lib/websocket.ts:27 — Server sends JSON.stringify({ type: 'output', data }) to terminal WS clients
apps/web/src/hooks/use-terminal.ts:52 — Client checks data.type === 'terminal:output', does not match 'output'
apps/web/src/hooks/use-terminal.ts:53 — Client reads data.payload.data but server has no 'payload' wrapper
apps/web/src/lib/websocket.ts:101 — WebSocketClient.onmessage parses JSON directly, no transformation

findings.notes: Wiring mismatch between server and client WebSocket message format

findings.description: Terminal router has no user isolation. All terminal operations (create, write, resize, kill, list, scrollback) are auth-protected but don't check if the calling user owns the terminal session. Any authenticated user can read/write/kill any terminal.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/terminal.ts:18 — create handler spawns terminal with no user association stored
packages/api/src/routers/terminal.ts:24 — list returns ALL sessions, not filtered by user
packages/api/src/routers/terminal.ts:31 — write accepts any sessionId, no ownership check
packages/api/src/routers/terminal.ts:52 — kill accepts any sessionId, no ownership check
packages/api/src/services/terminal-service.ts:4 — TerminalSession interface has no userId field

findings.notes: Missing authorization — any user can access any terminal session

findings.description: Learning router has no ownership checks. list, get, update, delete all accept any learning ID without verifying user ownership. Any authenticated user can read/modify/delete other users' learnings.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/learning.ts:60 — list returns findAll() unfiltered by user
packages/api/src/routers/learning.ts:72 — get returns any learning by ID, no ownership check
packages/api/src/routers/learning.ts:97 — update modifies any learning, no ownership check
packages/api/src/routers/learning.ts:107 — delete removes any learning, no ownership check

findings.notes: Missing authorization — IDOR vulnerability on learning resources

findings.description: Auto-mode endpoints (stop, status, setConcurrency, setConfig, getConfig) have no user/project ownership checks. AutoModeService is a singleton with one currentUserId — only one user can use auto-mode at a time. Any user can stop/configure another user's auto-mode.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/auto-mode.ts:60 — stop handler has no ownership check
packages/api/src/routers/auto-mode.ts:66 — status has no ownership check
packages/api/src/routers/auto-mode.ts:72 — setConcurrency has no ownership check
packages/api/src/routers/auto-mode.ts:86 — setConfig has no ownership check

findings.notes: Singleton design means only one user at a time — acceptable for desktop app but fragile

findings.description: Notification markRead and dismiss endpoints lack ownership verification. Other notification endpoints (list, countUnread, markAllRead) correctly verify project ownership, but markRead and dismiss accept any ID.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/notifications.ts:50 — markRead accepts any id, no ownership check
packages/api/src/routers/notifications.ts:67 — dismiss accepts any id, no ownership check

findings.notes: Inconsistent authorization — some endpoints check, others don't

findings.description: bulkCreate and bulkDelete in feature router use sequential loops WITHOUT transaction wrapping. If Nth operation fails, first N-1 are committed with no rollback. Errors silently caught and returned as success:false with no error detail.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/feature.ts:203 — bulkCreate iterates with for-of, each create independent, no transaction
packages/api/src/routers/feature.ts:224 — catch swallows error, returns { id: feat.title, success: false }
packages/api/src/routers/feature.ts:231 — bulkDelete has same pattern

findings.notes: Partial bulk operations can leave inconsistent state

findings.description: AgentService.listSessions() returns ALL sessions globally, router filters post-fetch. Inefficient and temporarily fetches data user shouldn't see. AutoModeService singleton supports only one concurrent user.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/agent.ts:96 — listSessions calls service.listSessions() which returns ALL, then filters by userId
packages/api/src/routers/session.ts:91 — Session list also fetches findAll() then filters
packages/api/src/services/auto-mode-service.ts:32 — currentUserId single field, one user at a time

findings.description: AC4 states database stored at .nomos/data/ but actual DB path is apps/server/data/nomos.db. AC is technically misleading but feature works.

evidence.detail: DB path configured as apps/server/data/nomos.db, not .nomos/data/

findings.notes: AC wording mismatch, not a code bug

findings.description: Kanban board missing 'failed' status column. KANBAN_COLUMNS defines 5 columns (backlog, pending, in_progress, waiting_approval, verified) — features with 'failed' status disappear from the board. Comment acknowledges intentional omission.

evidence.detail: apps/web/src/components/kanban/kanban-board.tsx:35 — Comment: 'failed' is valid but not shown
apps/web/src/components/kanban/kanban-board.tsx:40 — KANBAN_COLUMNS has 5 statuses, 'failed' omitted
packages/types/src/status.ts:76 — FEATURE_VALID_TRANSITIONS includes 'failed' as valid target

findings.notes: Features in 'failed' state become invisible on the board

findings.description: TanStack Router devtools and React Query devtools rendered unconditionally — visible in production builds, adds bundle size, exposes internal state.

evidence.detail: apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:99 — TanStackRouterDevtools rendered unconditionally, no import.meta.env.DEV check
apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:100 — ReactQueryDevtools rendered unconditionally
Screenshot 01-initial-login-page.png confirms TanStack Router devtools visible at bottom-left

findings.notes: Devtools visible in production — confirmed by runtime screenshot

findings.description: ID generation uses SELECT MAX(id) + padStart(3, '0'). After 999 entries, IDs become 4+ digits (F1000) breaking the F### branded pattern. No overflow guard exists.

evidence.detail: packages/db/src/lib/id-generation.ts:30 — padStart(3, '0'), after 999 IDs become 4+ digits
packages/db/src/lib/id-generation.ts:19 — Retry loop handles race conditions but no overflow check

findings.notes: Low priority — would only hit at 1000+ features/projects

findings.description: Settings router allows any authenticated user to read/write global scope settings. Acceptable for single-instance desktop app but would be vulnerability in multi-tenant deployment.

evidence.detail: packages/api/src/routers/settings.ts:50 — set with scope='global' has no ownership check
packages/api/src/routers/settings.ts:66 — getAll with scope='global' returns all settings to any user

findings.notes: Design decision — acceptable for current desktop-only scope
